Restrict this process with Landlock

Source: R/restrict.R
restrict_self.Rd

A thin wrapper over the kernel's Landlock interface for the calling process: the filesystem is denied except for the listed paths, TCP is restricted when tcp_bind or tcp_connect is given, and the scopes are applied. Irreversible. Landlock restricts the calling thread and what it creates afterwards, not threads that already exist; see confine().

Usage

restrict_self(
  read = NULL,
  write = NULL,
  exec = NULL,
  tcp_bind = NULL,
  tcp_connect = NULL,
  scope = c("signal", "abstract_unix"),
  best_effort = TRUE,
  log = NULL
)

Arguments

read, write, exec

Character vectors of paths; see fs().

tcp_bind, tcp_connect

Integer vectors of TCP ports, or NULL to leave TCP alone.

scope

Scopes to apply: any of "signal" and "abstract_unix".

best_effort, log

See policy().

Value

The report, invisibly; see apply_policy().
